newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European unions plan day of action on unemployment.
newsitem.headline: European unions plan day of action on unemployment.

text.p: European trade unions plan action across the continent on Wednesday to step up pressure on governments to create a social Europe in parallel with monetary union.

The Brussels-based European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) said it has called a "European Day of Action for Employment" with activities scheduled in more than 20 European countries, from Belgium to Bulgaria.
ETUC spokesman Wim Bergans said two million people may participate in the various events, ranging from demonstrations and concerts to seminars and debates.
Some 10,000 people are expected to form a human chain linking the buildings of the European Parliament, the European Commission and the European Union's Council of Ministers in Brussels.
"People have taken to the streets in favour of Europe, not against Europe," European Commission President Jacques Santer said in a statement. "That pleases me."
Santer said a social Europe already existed and was growing.
The action day follows worker rallies in western Europe in recent months against factory closures and industry restructuring as companies respond to intensifying competition.
The announcement in February by French car maker Renault of plans to shut down its Vilvoorde plant near Brussels with the loss of 3,100 jobs sparked angry demonstrations.

"There is no end in sight to the economic and social crisis and the accompanying reorganisations, privatisations and relocations which are undermining the structure of the economy and employment," ETUC said in a statement.
"The recent industrial conflicts across Europe clearly have shown that people will have nothing to do with a Union which disregards their legitimite employment and social policy aspirations."

Despite EU declarations about the need to bring down record unemployment, the EU jobless rate remained at 10.9 percent in March, which meant 18.3 million people in the 15-nation union were without jobs.
ETUC said Wednesday's action was intended to make the "workers' voice" heard at the EU's inter-governmental conference (IGC) on reform of the bloc's founding Treaty of Rome.
"The ETUC believes that the treaty must lay the foundations for a real Social Union which puts economic and employment policies on par with monetary policies," the statement said.
Bergans said ETUC was not against economic and monetary union (EMU). "But we are not unconditionally in favour."
Following the election victory of Britain's Labour Party, the EU's Amsterdam summit on June 16-17 is expected to agree to include a jobs chapter in the revised EU treaty.
Such a chapter would be intended to increase EU coordination on employment policies while leaving the responsibility for job creation firmly in the hands of national governments.

Trade unions may also be encouraged by the new British government's pledge to sign up to the EU's Social Chapter on worker rights and Sunday's strong socialist showing in the French parliament elections.
